title: Jump Game II
statement:
You are standing on index `0` of an array `nums` of `n` non-negative integers. From index `i` you may jump forward to any index `j` with `i < j ≤ i + nums[i]`. The value `nums[i]` is the **maximum** jump length from `i`; shorter jumps are also allowed. A value of `0` means you cannot move from that index.

Your goal is to reach the last index `n - 1`.

Decide whether this is possible and, if it is, find the **minimum number of jumps** needed. Print that number, or `-1` if the last index cannot be reached at all. If `n = 1` you are already at the last index, so the answer is `0`.

A dynamic-programming solution that tries every earlier index for each position is easy to write but too slow for the largest inputs. Interviewers usually want the greedy solution that runs in linear time.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `nums[0] ... nums[n-1]`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the minimum number of jumps to reach index `n - 1`, or `-1` if it is unreachable.

examples.explanation: Jump from index 0 to index 2 (length 2), then from index 2 to index 5 (length 3). One jump is not enough because index 0 only reaches indices 1 and 2.
From index 0 you can only reach index 1, and from index 1 only index 2. Index 2 holds 0, so you are stuck there and index 4 is never reached.
You already stand on the last index, so no jump is needed.

hints: Think in levels, like a BFS: all indices you can reach with 1 jump, then all indices reachable with 2 jumps, and so on. The set reachable with `j` jumps is always a contiguous range of indices.

While scanning, keep `cur_end`, the farthest index reachable with the current number of jumps, and `farthest`, the farthest index reachable with one more jump. When you pass `cur_end`, you must spend another jump and `cur_end` becomes `farthest`.
If you reach an index larger than `farthest` (or the scan ends with `farthest` still short of the last index), the end is unreachable and the answer is -1.

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
INF = float('inf')
dp = [INF] * n
dp[0] = 0
for i in range(1, n):
    for j in range(i):
        if j + a[j] >= i and dp[j] + 1 < dp[i]:
            dp[i] = dp[j] + 1
print(dp[n - 1] if dp[n - 1] != INF else -1)
